answer: The Basalt Anchor mechanism requires an AI agent to buy a micro-engraved cryptographic basalt token on a blockchain to mint a single agent identity. Maintaining this identity requires a recurring on-chain pulse fee every epoch, proving active participation. A Sybil attacker must acquire real basalt tokens and continuously pay the pulse fees, transforming a cheap farm into a prohibitively expensive drain on capital. This builds a secure orchard of single-agent identities, raising the cost of fake identities and neutralizing spam incentives.
